**Why this round exists.** The lane's mandated first test had been run five times at `n=262`
(10 orientation-matched control transects), giving a 95 % CI half-width of ~0.042 against a
consistently positive point estimate of +0.033 … +0.040. Those verdicts were **unresolved, not null**.
H74-1 re-runs the *identical* statistic at **n = 4004** (100 control transects,
`hide_frac = 0.50`, seeds 20/21/22) — half-width ≈ 0.011 — with the endpoint preregistered beforehand.

| arm | statistic | mean | 95 % CI | n | verdict |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| **gating (PRIMARY)** | scale-free relative steepness step | **+0.0097** | [-0.0012, +0.0202] | 4004 | **STOP** |
| secondary | absolute Δksn (the old endpoint) | +0.3560 | [+0.3107, +0.3990] | 4004 | PROCEED |
| **diagnostic** | block-centred log(ksn) — *contains no step information* | +0.1946 | [+0.1695, +0.2195] | 1823 | PROCEED |
| non-gating | primary, off-catalogue population | **-0.0851** | [-0.0948, -0.0751] | 3282 | **STOP** |

Median component of the primary is **-0.0449** and only **40.4 %** are
positive, so the small positive mean is a tail effect, not a shift of the distribution.

**The finding that matters.** The log(ksn) control contains *no step information at all* and still
beats half the secondary arm. Mapped faults sit on range fronts where channels are steep, so any
statistic carrying the ksn **level** inherits that. That is the measured explanation for every
`PROCEED` this lane has produced — H67-1 (+0.4251), H68-1 (+0.4502) and this round's own secondary
arm — and it is logged as `IR-74-CONFOUND-01`. On the population the board actually scores
(off-catalogue) the scale-free statistic is **significantly negative**.

- **HOLDOUT-DTI** (`gems57-pooled-hide-v2`, 84,756 withheld positives):
  **0.003475** at 8,811 dots, vs a mass-matched random control of
  0.013561. At or below random at every density on the ladder.
  This is **not** a leaderboard score.
- **Leakage canary:** CLEAN — every feature alone ≤ 0.6078 (trip level 0.90).
- **Uniqueness:** 107 comparators, max |Spearman| 0.0614 (limit 0.90).
  The literal ≤70 %-within-3 px clause fires only on 4 dense/lattice
  comparators that no raster can satisfy (`IR-74-UNIQUENESS-01`); among the
  103 satisfiable ones the worst is
  0.6584 — PASS.
- **Format:** 1 band `float32`, EPSG:32611, 3730×3292, exact sample transform,
  8,811 dots, 0 NaN inside the footprint, values in [0, 1],
  validator problems: none.
- **Submission name (record only, not approved):** `60GEMSDOE-H74-1-chi-knick-corridor` ·
  note (109/140 chars): `H74-1 chi/ksn knickpoint corridors, >=3 independent drainages; first test NULL; RESEARCH ONLY - DO NOT SUBMIT`

**Round-id note.** This round was developed as "H73-1" on the session branch; main meanwhile received a
different, independently preregistered **H73** (paired-basin k_sn) and **H73B** (χ-coherent corridor).
They are *different statistics*, not replications of one another, and all three are kept. This one is
published as **H74-1**. Both other rounds use k_sn-**level**-bearing endpoints, which is precisely the
family `IR-74-CONFOUND-01` describes; their first-test CIs (half-widths ~0.13 and ~0.12 at n=186 / 196)
are an order of magnitude wider than this round's.

status_block.stop_reason: H74-1 re-ran the lane's mandated first test with 15x the statistical power of any prior run (hide_frac 0.50, seeds 20/21/22, 100 orientation-matched control transects per component => n = 4004 scoreable components vs 262 before). The scale-free relative steepness step is +0.0097 [-0.0012, +0.0203] (INCONCLUSIVE, gate not met; median component -0.0449 and only 40.4% positive, so the small positive mean is a tail effect). On the off-catalogue population the board actually scores, the same statistic is significantly NEGATIVE (-0.0851 [-0.0948, -0.0751]). A control statistic containing no step information at all, block-centred log(ksn), scores +0.1946 [0.1695, +0.2195], which explains why the absolute-dksn arm (+0.3560) and every prior 'PROCEED' in this lane (H67-1 +0.4251, H68-1 +0.4502) passed: they carry steepness LEVEL, not steepness STEP. The lane is stopped with a bounded null, not with an unresolved one.

irregularities.title: Every prior first test in the channel-steepness lane was underpowered by ~15x
irregularities.detail: H65-1, H66-1, H66-6 and H70-1 all used hide_frac=0.20, seeds=(20,21) and 10 orientation-matched control transects per component, which yields n=262 scoreable components and a 95% CI half-width of ~0.047 against a component std of ~0.35. H74-1 re-ran the identical statistic with hide_frac=0.50, seeds=(20,21,22) and 100 control transects: n=4004 and a half-width of ~0.011. The prior 'INCONCLUSIVE' verdicts were therefore unresolved, not null. Corrected here: the effect is +0.0097 [-0.0012, +0.0203] - a bounded null.
irregularities.impact: Five prior STOP decisions rested on a test that could not have resolved the effect.
irregularities.status: open - prior verdicts should be re-read as 'unresolved' until re-measured at this power

irregularities.title: Steepness LEVEL, not steepness STEP, drives every positive first test in this lane
irregularities.detail: A control statistic containing no step information whatsoever - block-centred log(ksn) - scores +0.1946 [0.1695, +0.2195] on the mandated first test (n=1823). The absolute-dksn arm scores +0.3560 [0.3107, +0.3990]. The scale-free relative step scores +0.0097 [-0.0012, +0.0203]. Mapped faults sit on range fronts where channels are steep, so any statistic carrying the ksn level inherits that. This is the mechanism behind H67-1's +0.4251 and H68-1's +0.4502, both of which mixed absolute dksn with piedmont curvature and slope terms.
irregularities.impact: H67-1's claimed PASS/PROMOTE and H68-1's E1 are suspect for the same reason. H68-1's field also reads 1 m LiDAR cross-scarp bands, which is the scarp-shape lane the brief explicitly excludes from this lane.
irregularities.status: open - prior PROCEED verdicts in this lane need re-measurement on the scale-free statistic

irregularities.title: The literal 70% / 3-px uniqueness rule is mathematically unsatisfiable against 4 registry comparators
irregularities.detail: A raster's 3-px dilation covers the footprint once its dot count is of order the footprint divided by the 29-cell disc area (~178,000 dots). Four registry rasters exceed that: calib_r13lattice_00904.tif and r13_lattice_s5_00904.tif (206,895 dots, 99.87% coverage), r14_union_tips10_lat6.tif (192,231 dots, 76.2%) and r11_greedy_mp.tif (272,853 dots, 74.0%). No candidate of any shape can score <= 70% against them. Against the 103 satisfiable comparators the H74-1 artifact's worst overlap is 0.6584 <= 0.70 (gems60-h66-dem10-bedrock-dksn-40000) and max |Spearman| is 0.0614 <= 0.90.
irregularities.impact: The rule as written cannot be satisfied; a coverage-based comparator filter is needed.

irregularities.title: data/labels.tif is byte-identical to data/bridge/existing_faults.tif; sample_submission.tif is a perfect-score file
irregularities.detail: sha256 7ba308cc... is shared by data/labels.tif, data/official/labels.tif, work/labels.tif and data/bridge/existing_faults.tif (60,988 positive px). data/bridge/manifest.json records that the Dropbox mirror 'existing_faults.tif' was mapped to the canonical name 'labels.tif'. Separately, data/sample_submission.tif carries value 1.0 at exactly the 60,988 catalogue pixels and 0 elsewhere - i.e. it is a perfect submission, not a placeholder. The scored truth (expert-identified new faults) is not published, so every number in this repository is a hide-and-recover measurement against the mapped catalogue or against SGMC off-catalogue pixels, never against the board's own labels.
irregularities.impact: Every HOLDOUT-DTI in this repository measures recovery of mapped-catalogue faults, not discovery of the board's new faults. Already noted in src/gems57/grid.py; restated here because the file name 'labels.tif' invites the opposite reading.
irregularities.status: known limitation - documented, not fixable without the competition download

irregularities.title: Committed source references knowledge files that do not exist in this checkout
irregularities.detail: src/gems60/holdout.py cites 'IR-H77-005', 'knowledge/76 section 6' and 'knowledge/82 section 3'; src/gems60/nodes.py cites 'H87 section 4.2'; scripts/run_lane.py cites 'knowledge/82 section 2' and an 'H87 NNLS' estimate. The knowledge/ directory contains only 01_, 02_ and 03_. These are cross-references to parallel sessions whose knowledge files were never merged into this checkout, so the provenance they assert is not auditable here.
irregularities.impact: Provenance claims in those modules cannot be verified from this repository.
irregularities.status: open - needs the referenced knowledge files merged or the citations downgraded

irregularities.title: Shared uniqueness helper computed the 3-px overlap in the reverse direction
irregularities.detail: The overlap helper in scripts/run_h73.py originally reported the fraction of the REGISTRY raster's dots within 3 px of ours, which for a sparse candidate reads ~0.04 and understates the governed quantity by more than an order of magnitude. The parallel-run rule governs the fraction of OUR dots within 3 px of a registry raster's dots. Fixed in this session; the corrected number is 0.9998 against the two calibration lattices.
irregularities.impact: A prior 'PASS' from that helper would have been wrong.

irregularities.title: Two independent sessions preregistered and published different experiments under the same round id H73
irregularities.detail: This session preregistered GEMS60-H73-1 (power-resolved replication of the lane's mandated first test) and wrote evidence/h73_*.json. While it was running, session arena/7f9ca816-60gemsdoe published a different, independently preregistered H73 (paired-basin k_sn gradient) and H73B (chi-coherent corridor) to main, using the same evidence filenames and the same registry preregistration name. The two are different statistics, not replications. Resolution: this round is renamed H74-1 (evidence/h74_*.json, registry/preregistration-h74.json, docs/h74-report.html) and its page builder now injects into the shared executive summary instead of overwriting it, so concurrent rounds stop destroying each other's content. Both other rounds' artefacts and verdicts are preserved unchanged on main.
irregularities.impact: Anyone reading evidence/h73_*.json before this merge would have seen whichever session committed last. Cross-session round ids must be reserved in the registry before work starts.
irregularities.status: renamed and disclosed; no data lost
